messages:
luca: Quick follow-up from the SM-capability RFC — we saw inconsistent perf across A100/H100/L4 when we gate WMMA kernels. Need a clear runtime policy. Observed: H100 gets ~1.9x on long seq with wmma_fp16, A100 still wins on small-batch dense due to occupancy, L4 has no tensor cores so fp16 path is much slower. Thoughts on JIT vs precompile, gating API, and how many kernel variants we keep? (cc @sima @raj @mia)

sima: Ran a focused microbench last night. Short summary: H100 (p4d) w/ `wmma_fp16` -> 1.9x for seq=2048/batch=8; A100 w/ `wmma_bf16` -> ~1.3x for long seq, BUT for batch=1/seq=128 the *generic fp16* path was ~20% faster on A100. L4 (low-power) has no tensor cores -> fallback `fp16_no_wmma` is ~2.4x slower than H100-wmma. Uploaded raw CSV to the perf gist: https://perf.internal/gists/176950

raj: API thought: runtime should query sm_capabilities (tensorcore/bf16/int8/dp4a) and we keep a policy table keyed by (model_profile, seq_len_range, batch_range, sm_caps) -> kernel_id. Kernel selection should be pure: `kernel_selector.select(model_profile, workload)` that returns kernel_id + resource_estimate. Keep kernel signatures stable.

mia: Policy table makes sense. Concern: binary size explosion if we precompile every variant. Proposal: Hosted service -> precompile the top N combos (H100/A100 common configs), fallback to JIT for exotic combos. Dedicated/Private -> let customer opt-in to precompile at deploy time (flag `precompile_kernels: true`).

engbot: perf-ci: recent run 1769504300 added `wmma_fp16` path. Quick output:
```
{ "test": "wmma_path_longseq", "h100": 1.92, "a100": 1.31, "l4": 0.45 }
```
Full logs: https://perf.internal/reports/1769504300 (contains kernel launch traces + SASS counters)

natalie: Heads-up about correctness: bf16->fp16 or WMMA rounding can change logits in subtle ways. We need a deterministic eval-suite per model family to catch quality regressions. Also watch for NaNs when using aggressive int8 paths.

luca: +1 on deterministic evals. Also we need runtime safety nets: if kernel returns NaNs or violates invariants -> capture dump, switch to fallback kernel, and alert. That fallback must be automatic with throttled alerts (no noise).

sima: I'll run a nightly sweep across H100/A100/L4 images and push a perf+error CSV to the perf bucket. Will include tests for async-copy vs shared-mem variants and also measure occupancy/regs usage.

raj: Implementation note: keep selection logic in a single module `kernel_selector`. It should expose a register API: `register_kernel(kernel_id, predicate_fn, metadata)` where `predicate_fn(sm_caps, profile)` is evaluated at selection time. Selector returns `(kernel_id, expected_resources)` and doesn't launch anything. This keeps side-effect-free selection and easier testing.

mia: Rollout plan idea: canary at 5% traffic with strict SLO gating (p50/p95/p99 latency + token-accuracy evals). If any model-family sees >1% correctness delta or latency tail regressions, auto rollback.

luca: OK. Action items:
- @sima run perf sweep and post CSV by EOD tomorrow
- @raj prototype `kernel_selector` + predicate API (small PR)
- @mia write canary + rollback plan and required metrics
I'll open a short RFC PR merging these decisions and include the perf table + example gating config. Thanks everyone :pray:
